decisions.situation: A financial or safety rule must hold every time
decisions.choose: A hook or programmatic gate
decisions.why: Code is deterministic; a prompt instruction fails some of the time

decisions.situation: A best-effort style or tone preference
decisions.choose: A system-prompt instruction
decisions.why: Occasional misses are acceptable, so enforcement would be over-engineering

decisions.situation: Normalise mixed tool-result formats (timestamps, units)
decisions.choose: A PostToolUse hook
decisions.why: It transforms results deterministically before the model sees them

decisions.situation: A multi-file or architectural change with several valid approaches
decisions.choose: Plan mode
decisions.why: Explore and agree on an approach before editing many files

decisions.situation: A clear, single-file fix
decisions.choose: Direct execution
decisions.why: Plan mode only adds overhead for well-scoped changes

decisions.situation: The model must call some tool, but may pick which
decisions.choose: tool_choice "any"
decisions.why: "auto" may return text; forcing removes the choice

decisions.situation: A specific tool must run first
decisions.choose: Forced tool_choice {"type":"tool","name":...}
decisions.why: Guarantees that exact call on that request

decisions.situation: A workflow blocks on the result (pre-merge check, live chat)
decisions.choose: Synchronous API
decisions.why: Batches have no latency SLA and can take up to 24 hours

decisions.situation: A latency-tolerant job (overnight report, weekly audit)
decisions.choose: Message Batches API
decisions.why: About 50% cheaper when nothing waits on the result

decisions.situation: Match batch results to inputs and resubmit failures
decisions.choose: A custom_id on every request
decisions.why: Results aren't returned in input order

decisions.situation: A subagent fails
decisions.choose: Return structured error context (type, query, partial results, alternatives)
decisions.why: The coordinator can recover instead of aborting or guessing

decisions.situation: A subagent needs earlier findings or requirements
decisions.choose: Pass them explicitly in its prompt
decisions.why: Subagents have isolated context and inherit nothing

decisions.situation: Subagents need to share findings
decisions.choose: Route them through the coordinator
decisions.why: Hub-and-spoke keeps the system observable and errors handled consistently

decisions.situation: The customer explicitly asks for a human
decisions.choose: Escalate immediately
decisions.why: An explicit request is a trigger; don't try to resolve first

decisions.situation: A frustrated customer with a simple issue
decisions.choose: Acknowledge, offer to resolve, escalate if they ask again
decisions.why: Sentiment isn't complexity

decisions.situation: A lookup returns several matching customers
decisions.choose: Ask for another identifier
decisions.why: Acting on a heuristic guess risks the wrong account

decisions.situation: A long conversation is losing amounts, dates and IDs
decisions.choose: A persistent case-facts block
decisions.why: Progressive summarisation drops exact values

decisions.situation: A tool can't reach its source vs finds nothing
decisions.choose: Return isError for the failure; a success with no results for a true empty
decisions.why: Otherwise the agent treats an outage as "nothing exists"

decisions.situation: An agent has too many tools and picks wrongly
decisions.choose: Cut to about 4–5 tools scoped to its role
decisions.why: Selection reliability falls as tool count grows

decisions.situation: Two tools with overlapping descriptions get confused
decisions.choose: Rewrite or rename the descriptions to remove overlap
decisions.why: Descriptions are the main selection signal; fix them before adding layers

decisions.situation: Find files by name pattern vs search file contents
decisions.choose: Glob for names; Grep for contents
decisions.why: Each is built for one job

decisions.situation: Team-wide vs personal Claude Code config
decisions.choose: Committed project files vs ~/.claude or settings.local.json
decisions.why: Only project files reach teammates through git

decisions.situation: A team MCP server vs a personal one
decisions.choose: Project .mcp.json with ${VAR} vs ~/.claude.json
decisions.why: Shared config is committed; secrets come from env vars

decisions.situation: Conventions for one file type spread across many folders
decisions.choose: A .claude/rules/ file with a paths glob
decisions.why: A subdirectory CLAUDE.md only covers its own folder

decisions.situation: A skill whose verbose output shouldn't flood the conversation
decisions.choose: context: fork in SKILL.md frontmatter
decisions.why: It runs in an isolated sub-agent and returns only the result

decisions.situation: A field is often absent and the model invents values
decisions.choose: Make it optional and nullable
decisions.why: The model can return null instead of fabricating

decisions.situation: Retry an extraction: format error vs missing data
decisions.choose: Retry with the specific errors for format; don't retry missing data
decisions.why: Retries can't find what the source doesn't contain

decisions.situation: Reviewing generated code
decisions.choose: An independent instance or fresh session
decisions.why: The generating session keeps its reasoning and rarely questions it

decisions.situation: A large PR review misses issues
decisions.choose: Per-file passes plus a cross-file integration pass
decisions.why: Avoids diluting attention across everything

decisions.situation: Deciding whether to reduce human review
decisions.choose: Accuracy segmented by document type and field
decisions.why: An aggregate can hide one failing segment

decisions.situation: Resume a session vs start fresh
decisions.choose: Resume if context is mostly valid (say what changed); start fresh with a summary if results are stale
decisions.why: Stale tool results mislead the model

decisions.situation: Compare two approaches from the same analysis
decisions.choose: fork_session
decisions.why: Branches share the baseline but stay independent

decisions.situation: Synthesis from sources that disagree
decisions.choose: Keep claim-source mappings; report both values with attribution
decisions.why: Picking one silently loses provenance

decisions.situation: Decide when the agentic loop ends
decisions.choose: Check stop_reason: continue on "tool_use", stop on "end_turn"
decisions.why: Text that sounds finished isn't a signal; an iteration cap is only a backstop

decisions.situation: A tool call fails mid-loop
decisions.choose: Return its tool_result with the error text and is_error: true
decisions.why: The model can adapt instead of the run ending

decisions.situation: The next tool depends on what earlier results show
decisions.choose: Give Claude the tools and let it choose each call
decisions.why: A fixed keyword decision tree can't react to findings

decisions.situation: The steps are known in advance (multi-aspect review, fixed pipeline)
decisions.choose: A fixed prompt chain with code checks between steps
decisions.why: Dynamic decomposition adds flexibility the task doesn't need

decisions.situation: Open-ended investigation where you don't know where the answer is
decisions.choose: Map the structure, rank high-impact areas, adapt the plan as findings arrive
decisions.why: A fixed plan can't follow what each step finds

decisions.situation: Investigation steps depend on each other's findings
decisions.choose: Keep them in one context
decisions.why: Pipeline subagents lose details at each handoff; use them for independent lookups

decisions.situation: Prose requests keep fixing one input and breaking another
decisions.choose: Give exact failing inputs and expected outputs as test cases
decisions.why: Concrete cases pin down what the prose leaves open

decisions.situation: Several problems to report
decisions.choose: Interacting ones together in one message; independent ones in separate, sequential messages
decisions.why: Interacting fixes need each other's context; independent ones stay focused

decisions.situation: CI needs machine-parseable review output
decisions.choose: --json-schema with a findings schema
decisions.why: Prompt wording and output cleanup aren't guaranteed

decisions.situation: CI review gives false positives and repeats findings on re-runs
decisions.choose: Explicit review criteria in CLAUDE.md; pass prior findings on re-runs
decisions.why: Claude reports what the criteria cover and skips what's already known

decisions.situation: Written rules don't separate acceptable from genuine cases
decisions.choose: 2–4 varied examples with reasoning, including a case to skip
decisions.why: Examples show where the line is; a single example fixes only one case

decisions.situation: Extraction returns null fields because document layouts vary
decisions.choose: A few examples across the real formats, including one where null is correct
decisions.why: Examples teach the layouts; the null case stops fabrication

decisions.situation: A long exploration is losing earlier findings
decisions.choose: Write key findings to a scratchpad file and check it before answering
decisions.why: Context degrades over a long session; the file doesn't

decisions.situation: A session is full of verbose output but the work must continue
decisions.choose: /compact with an instruction naming the findings to keep
decisions.why: Clearing or handing off loses the reasoning so far

decisions.situation: The next exploration phase runs in new subagents
decisions.choose: Summarise the phase's key findings into their prompts
decisions.why: Subagents inherit nothing from the parent

alwaysWrong.text: Parsing natural-language phrases ("done", "complete") to end the agent loop
alwaysWrong.why: Text is unreliable; the loop should be controlled by stop_reason

alwaysWrong.text: An iteration cap as the main stopping rule
alwaysWrong.why: A cap guesses task length; keep it only as a safety net beside stop_reason

alwaysWrong.text: Enforcing a critical rule with a prompt instruction
alwaysWrong.why: Prompts are probabilistic; use a hook, gate or schema

alwaysWrong.text: Escalating on the model's self-reported confidence
alwaysWrong.why: Self-confidence is poorly calibrated; use explicit escalation criteria

alwaysWrong.text: Escalating on customer sentiment
alwaysWrong.why: Sentiment doesn't measure case complexity or policy gaps

alwaysWrong.text: Generic error messages like "Operation failed"
alwaysWrong.why: The agent can't choose a recovery; return category and retryability

alwaysWrong.text: Silently suppressing errors or returning empty success
alwaysWrong.why: A failure looks like a valid empty result; return isError

alwaysWrong.text: Giving one agent many tools "for convenience"
alwaysWrong.why: Selection degrades; scope about 4–5 tools to the role

alwaysWrong.text: Same-session self-review
alwaysWrong.why: The generator keeps its reasoning; use an independent instance

alwaysWrong.text: Trusting aggregate metrics
alwaysWrong.why: Averages hide per-type and per-field failures; segment them

alwaysWrong.text: Adding a classifier, router or extra agent to fix tool confusion or enforce one check
alwaysWrong.why: Fix the root cause with the smallest change: clearer descriptions, a prerequisite gate

alwaysWrong.text: Team standards in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, or a personal MCP server in the committed .mcp.json
alwaysWrong.why: Only committed project files reach teammates; personal config goes in ~/.claude or .local files

alwaysWrong.text: Clearing the conversation or restarting when context runs low
alwaysWrong.why: Values the user already gave are lost; compact into a case-facts block or resume

alwaysWrong.text: Raising max_tokens to fit a longer document
alwaysWrong.why: max_tokens caps output length, not the context window

alwaysWrong.text: Subagents passing results straight to each other or through a shared store
alwaysWrong.why: Route everything through the coordinator so it stays observable and handles errors

alwaysWrong.text: Aborting the whole workflow because one source or document failed
alwaysWrong.why: Recover locally, continue with partial results, and report the gap

alwaysWrong.text: Running a pre-merge check or live chat through the Message Batches API
alwaysWrong.why: Batches have no latency SLA (up to 24 hours); blocking work is synchronous

alwaysWrong.text: Telling a subagent to "use the findings above"
alwaysWrong.why: Subagents inherit nothing; put the findings in its prompt

alwaysWrong.text: An invented flag or config key (--non-interactive, subagent_inherit_context)
alwaysWrong.why: Made-up features are always wrong; use the documented mechanism, such as -p for CI

alwaysWrong.text: Escalating after one transient tool error or a routine in-policy request
alwaysWrong.why: Retry or resolve what the agent can; escalate on explicit criteria

alwaysWrong.text: Continuing to troubleshoot after the customer asks for a person
alwaysWrong.why: An explicit request for a human is an immediate trigger

alwaysWrong.text: Blaming a subagent that did everything it was assigned
alwaysWrong.why: Rule out what the evidence clears; look at what owns the gap (decomposition, prompt, handoff)

alwaysWrong.text: Resuming a session and trusting its old tool readings
alwaysWrong.why: They may no longer match the current state; start fresh with a summary and re-run live checks

alwaysWrong.text: Running independent tasks one after another when the deadline needs them together
alwaysWrong.why: Spawn them in parallel: several Task calls in one coordinator response

alwaysWrong.text: Averaging two conflicting credible values, or picking one
alwaysWrong.why: Keep both with their sources and methods, and mark the finding as contested

items: 60 questions in 120 minutes, closed book
Scaled score 100–1000; 720 passes (not the same as 72%)
No guessing penalty; unanswered questions count as wrong
4 of the 6 scenarios are drawn at random
Single-answer questions have 4 options; multiple-response questions also appear
Domain weights: D1 27%, D2 18%, D3 20%, D4 20%, D5 15%
$125, valid 12 months; up to 4 attempts in 12 months, with waits of 14, 30 and 90 days
CLAUDE.md: user ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, project .claude/CLAUDE.md or root CLAUDE.md, and subdirectory files; concatenated from broadest to most specific
@import pulls in other files; .claude/rules/*.md with paths frontmatter load only for matching files
Commands: .claude/commands/ (project, shared) vs ~/.claude/commands/ (personal)
Skills: .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md with frontmatter such as context: fork, allowed-tools, argument-hint
MCP: .mcp.json (project, ${VAR} expansion) vs ~/.claude.json (user)
Settings: .claude/settings.json is committed and shared; .claude/settings.local.json is personal; permissions go under permissions.allow
/memory shows which memory files are loaded
-p / --print runs non-interactively
--output-format json for machine-readable output
--json-schema to constrain the output shape
--resume <session-name> continues a named session
fork_session branches from a shared baseline
"auto": the model may call a tool or reply with text
"any": the model must call a tool, but chooses which
{"type":"tool","name":"..."}: the model must call that specific tool
About 50% cheaper; results within up to 24 hours; no latency SLA
No multi-turn tool calling within one request
custom_id matches results to requests and lets you resubmit only failures
Refine the prompt on a sample before submitting the full batch
Set submission frequency from the SLA (e.g. a 30-hour SLA → submit in 4-hour windows)
stop_reason "tool_use": run the requested tools and send the results back
stop_reason "end_turn": the model has finished; this ends the loop, not text like "done"
stop_reason "max_tokens": the output was cut off and isn't a finished answer
Every tool_use block gets its own tool_result, matched by tool_use_id
A failed tool still returns a tool_result, with the error text and is_error: true
Each request carries the full history, tool results included
An iteration cap is a safety net set well above normal work, not the stopping rule
Subagents have isolated context: pass what they need in the prompt; only their final message comes back
Spawn independent subagents in parallel with several Task calls in one coordinator response
All subagent communication goes through the coordinator (hub-and-spoke)
/compact with an instruction naming what to keep shrinks a long session without losing key findings
A scratchpad file holds key findings across a long exploration
context: fork in SKILL.md runs the skill in an isolated sub-agent and returns only the result
Tool use with a JSON schema gives schema-valid output, not correct values
Make often-absent fields optional and nullable so the model can return null instead of inventing
Retry with the specific validation errors; retries can't find data the source doesn't contain
Few-shot: 2–4 varied examples covering each kind of input, including a case to skip or a correct null
Escalate at once on an explicit request for a human, a policy exception or gap, or no progress
Not triggers on their own: negative sentiment or the model's self-reported confidence
Several matching customers: ask for another identifier instead of guessing
A frustrated customer with a simple issue: acknowledge, offer to resolve, escalate if they ask again
